note: A CLIENT SMOKE TEST CAN PARSE PROSE, AND NOTHING LOCAL WILL TELL YOU. The Rhumb changed one player-facing sentence in windows/vessel (the exits listing) and the stage gate held on clients rc=2. Cause: clients/vessel/wasm/drive.mjs walked the character by PARSING a direction out of the opening text — golden.match(/^Ways on: (.+)\.m) — and the campaign had deleted that sentence. The regex matched nothing and the driver died on its own assertion. WHY NOTHING LOCAL SAW IT: clients/ is outside the cargo workspace with its own toolchains, so make vessel-check is in NONE of the three gates, and there is no CI (0125). gate-commit was 1425/1425, docs_consistency 23/23, drift clean — all green, all blind to it. The campaign had diligently regenerated clients/game/core/tests/fixtures/ and never run the SIBLING clients smoke test. The generated-artifact discipline covers committed fixtures; it says nothing about a hand-written driver that PARSES one. THE REUSABLE RULE: a test that derives its input by parsing human-facing prose has a dependency the type system cannot see and no drift check will ever report, because the prose is ALLOWED to change. Before rewriting a player-facing sentence, grep clients/ for it — a symbol grep will not find it, because the coupling is to a STRING. ATTRIBUTION METHOD worth copying: do not assume a held phase is yours. A/B the committed artifact against main — Ways on: appears 8x in mains transcript and 2x in ours, and both survivors were chamber-band prose we never touched. That is a 10-second check that turns a guess into a fact.
